title: Cloud services, anti-patterns and the ADR
summary: The managed options and their exact semantics, the designs reviewers push back on, and writing the decision down as an architecture decision record.

steps.title: The managed options
body: | Service | Shape | The semantics you must know |

| **Azure Service Bus** | queues; topics with subscriptions (filters) | peek-lock with a lock duration; **sessions** (`SessionId`) for FIFO per key; `MaxDeliveryCount` (default 10) then the built-in dead-letter subqueue; duplicate detection window; scheduled messages |

| **Azure Event Hubs** | partitioned log | consumer groups; **checkpoints** (the processor stores them in Blob Storage); time-based retention; a **Kafka-compatible endpoint** (port 9093) for Kafka clients |

| **Amazon SQS** | queue | **standard**: at-least-once, best-effort order; **FIFO**: `MessageGroupId` for order, `MessageDeduplicationId` (5-minute window); **visibility timeout** (default 30 s); redrive policy with `maxReceiveCount` to a DLQ; long polling up to 20 s |
| **Amazon SNS** | pub/sub | fans out to SQS queues (one per subscriber), Lambda, HTTP; filter policies; FIFO topics pair with FIFO queues |
| **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams** | partitioned log | shards with per-shard write limits; partition key to shard; retention from 24 hours up to 365 days; consumers checkpoint (KCL uses DynamoDB) |
| **Amazon MSK** | managed Kafka | real Kafka (provisioned or serverless); your Kafka skills and clients apply |

| **Google Cloud Pub/Sub** | topics and subscriptions | **ack deadline** (default 10 s, extendable); **ordering keys**; dead-letter topics with max delivery attempts; seek to a timestamp or snapshot to replay retained messages |
Google Cloud also offers a managed Apache Kafka service, and Confluent Cloud runs Kafka on all three clouds. Read the
quotas page of whichever you pick: per-partition, per-shard and per-group throughput limits decide your sizing.

steps.prompt: Match each setting to what it controls.
pairs: FIFO per key; one receiver holds a session at a time
How long a received message stays hidden before another consumer can receive it
Receives before the message moves to the dead-letter queue
A consumer's saved position in a partition, like a committed offset
Time to ack before Pub/Sub delivers the message again
Drops a resend with the same id within 5 minutes
explain: The same four ideas recur in every product under different names: a lease (lock duration, visibility timeout, ack
deadline), a retry limit, a dead-letter destination and a position (offset, checkpoint).

steps.prompt: Every video is transcoded about three times. Jobs take around 90 s. What is the cause and the fix?
options: The visibility timeout (30 s) is shorter than the job, so the message reappears and another worker takes it; raise it above the worst-case job time or extend it with `ChangeMessageVisibility` while working, and keep the worker idempotent
SQS standard queues always deliver three copies; switch to FIFO
`maxReceiveCount` 5 makes SQS deliver each message five times
explain: The receive count of 3 and 412 messages "not visible" give it away: workers keep re-receiving jobs that are still
running. FIFO would not help; the lease is simply too short. The same bug exists as a Service Bus lock that expires
(`MessageLockLostException`) and a Pub/Sub ack deadline that passes.

steps.title: Anti-patterns a reviewer will catch
body: - **Kafka as a task queue with per-message acks.** Committing each record by hand does not make Kafka a queue: a
slow record still blocks its partition, parallelism stops at the partition count, and jobs longer than
`max.poll.interval.ms` trigger rebalances. Use a queue (or evaluate share groups on a version that supports them).
- **RabbitMQ as a long-term event store.** Millions of messages parked in a queue "for later" eat memory and disk,
trigger alarms that block publishers, and still cannot be replayed once acked. Use a stream or a log.
- **A database table as a queue without `SKIP LOCKED`.** Workers that `SELECT ... LIMIT 1` then `UPDATE` take the
same row; with plain `FOR UPDATE` they queue up behind each other. Done right it is a perfectly good queue at
moderate volume, and it pairs naturally with the outbox:
```sql
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', locked_by = 'worker-3', locked_at = now()
WHERE id = (
SELECT id FROM jobs
WHERE status = 'ready'
ORDER BY id
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
LIMIT 1)
RETURNING id, payload;
Add an index on `(status, id)` and a sweeper that resets rows whose `locked_at` is older than the job timeout.
- **One queue or topic per customer** (millions of them): every broker has per-queue or per-partition overhead.
Use a key, a session or a header instead.

items: A Kafka topic of 20-minute video jobs, committing each offset by hand
A RabbitMQ queue holding 90 days of events for consumers that do not exist yet
A Postgres `jobs` table claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` at 50 jobs per second
Workers that `SELECT ... WHERE status = 'ready' LIMIT 1`, then `UPDATE` the row
A 7-day Kafka event stream that three teams consume
An SQS standard queue for thumbnail jobs with idempotent workers
One RabbitMQ queue per customer, two million queues
explain: Most anti-patterns are a reasonable tool used for the other shape: a log used as a queue, a queue used as a log, a
table used as a queue without the one clause that makes it safe.

steps.title: Write it down: the ADR
body: A design review ends in an **architecture decision record**: a short Markdown file in the repository
(`docs/adr/0057-messaging-backbone.md`) that says what was decided and why, so the next engineer does not reopen the
debate without new facts.
```text
# ADR-57: Messaging backbone for the returns platform
Status: Proposed
## Context        what we need, with numbers: 4,000 msg/s peak, 6 consumer teams, 30-day replay,
per-return ordering, label jobs of 2-4 minutes, Azure, two engineers know RabbitMQ
## Options        the candidates, scored with the SAME weights and knock-outs
## Decision       one or two sentences: "Event Hubs for return events; Service Bus queues for label jobs."
## Consequences   what gets easier, what gets harder, what it costs, who runs it
## Revisit when   the signal that changes the answer: "replay needs beyond 90 days", "a second cloud"
A good ADR is honest about the losing options and the costs of the winner. "We chose Kafka because it is the
industry standard" is not a reason; "replay for 30 days by six teams, which queues cannot do" is.

steps.prompt: Put the sections of the ADR in order.
lines: Context: the requirements, with numbers and constraints
Options considered, scored against the same criteria
Decision: what we will do, in one or two sentences
Consequences: what gets easier, what gets harder, what it costs
Revisit when: the signal that would change the decision
steps.explain: Context before options keeps the scoring honest: the criteria come from the requirements, not from the favourite.

steps.title: Pick the managed service
prompt: Map a requirement set to a managed service, with reasons. The tests define
```csharp
record Need(string Cloud, bool Log, bool OrderedPerKey, bool KafkaApi, bool FanOut);
Write `(string Service, List<string> Reasons) PickManaged(Need n)`. `Cloud` is `"aws"`, `"azure"` or `"gcp"`;
anything else throws `ArgumentException`. Reasons are added only when their condition is true, in the order listed.
**aws**
- `KafkaApi` → `"Amazon MSK"`: `"Kafka protocol: existing clients work unchanged"`
- else `Log` → `"Amazon Kinesis Data Streams"`: `"partitioned log with replay"`; `OrderedPerKey` → `"ordering per partition key"`
- else `FanOut` → `"Amazon SNS FIFO + SQS FIFO"` if `OrderedPerKey`, otherwise `"Amazon SNS + SQS"`:
`"SNS fans out to one SQS queue per subscriber"`; `OrderedPerKey` → `"message group id keeps per-key order"`
- else → `"Amazon SQS FIFO"` if `OrderedPerKey`, otherwise `"Amazon SQS"`: `OrderedPerKey` →
`"message group id keeps per-key order"`; always `"redrive to a dead-letter queue after maxReceiveCount"`
**azure**
- `KafkaApi` or `Log` → `"Azure Event Hubs"`: `KafkaApi` → `"Kafka endpoint: existing clients work with a config change"`;
`Log` → `"partitioned log with consumer groups and checkpoints"`; `OrderedPerKey` → `"ordering per partition key"`
- else → `"Azure Service Bus"`: `FanOut` → `"topic with one subscription per consumer"`; `OrderedPerKey` →
`"sessions keep per-key order"`; always `"dead-letter queue after MaxDeliveryCount"`
**gcp**
- `KafkaApi` → `"Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka"`: `"Kafka protocol: existing clients work unchanged"`
- else → `"Google Cloud Pub/Sub"`: `FanOut` → `"one subscription per consumer"`; `OrderedPerKey` → `"ordering keys"`;
`Log` → `"seek to a timestamp to replay retained messages"`; always `"dead-letter topic after max delivery attempts"`
solution: return ("Amazon MSK", new List<string> { "Kafka protocol: existing clients work unchanged" });
reasons.Add("SNS fans out to one SQS queue per subscriber");
if (n.OrderedPerKey) reasons.Add("message group id keeps per-key order");
return (n.OrderedPerKey ? "Amazon SNS FIFO + SQS FIFO" : "Amazon SNS + SQS", reasons);
if (n.OrderedPerKey) reasons.Add("message group id keeps per-key order");
reasons.Add("redrive to a dead-letter queue after maxReceiveCount");
if (n.KafkaApi) reasons.Add("Kafka endpoint: existing clients work with a config change");
if (n.Log) reasons.Add("partitioned log with consumer groups and checkpoints");
if (n.FanOut) reasons.Add("topic with one subscription per consumer");
return ("Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka", new List<string> { "Kafka protocol: existing clients work unchanged" });
if (n.Log) reasons.Add("seek to a timestamp to replay retained messages");
reasons.Add("dead-letter topic after max delivery attempts");
hints: A `switch (n.Cloud)` with one case per cloud, each checking the conditions in the listed order.
Build a `reasons` list as you go and return it with the service name.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoA = PickManaged(new Need("aws", Log: false, OrderedPerKey: true, KafkaApi: false, FanOut: false));
Dojo.Eq("aws ordered work queue", "Amazon SQS FIFO", dojoA.Service);
Dojo.Eq("aws ordered work queue: reasons", new List<string> { "message group id keeps per-key order", "redrive to a dead-letter queue after maxReceiveCount" }, dojoA.Reasons);
var dojoB = PickManaged(new Need("aws", false, false, false, true));
Dojo.Eq("aws fan-out", "Amazon SNS + SQS", dojoB.Service);
Dojo.Eq("aws fan-out: reasons", new List<string> { "SNS fans out to one SQS queue per subscriber" }, dojoB.Reasons);
Dojo.Eq("aws ordered fan-out", "Amazon SNS FIFO + SQS FIFO", PickManaged(new Need("aws", false, true, false, true)).Service);
var dojoC = PickManaged(new Need("aws", true, true, false, true));
Dojo.Eq("aws log wins over fan-out", "Amazon Kinesis Data Streams", dojoC.Service);
Dojo.Eq("aws log: reasons", new List<string> { "partitioned log with replay", "ordering per partition key" }, dojoC.Reasons);
Dojo.Eq("aws Kafka API", "Amazon MSK", PickManaged(new Need("aws", true, true, true, true)).Service);
var dojoD = PickManaged(new Need("azure", true, true, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("azure Kafka clients and a log", "Azure Event Hubs", dojoD.Service);

Dojo.Eq("azure Event Hubs: reasons", new List<string> { "Kafka endpoint: existing clients work with a config change", "partitioned log with consumer groups and checkpoints", "ordering per partition key" }, dojoD.Reasons);
var dojoE = PickManaged(new Need("azure", false, true, false, true));
Dojo.Eq("azure ordered fan-out", "Azure Service Bus", dojoE.Service);
Dojo.Eq("azure Service Bus: reasons", new List<string> { "topic with one subscription per consumer", "sessions keep per-key order", "dead-letter queue after MaxDeliveryCount" }, dojoE.Reasons);
var dojoF = PickManaged(new Need("gcp", true, true, false, true));
Dojo.Eq("gcp", "Google Cloud Pub/Sub", dojoF.Service);

Dojo.Eq("gcp: reasons", new List<string> { "one subscription per consumer", "ordering keys", "seek to a timestamp to replay retained messages", "dead-letter topic after max delivery attempts" }, dojoF.Reasons);
Dojo.Eq("gcp Kafka API", "Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka", PickManaged(new Need("gcp", false, false, true, false)).Service);
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("unknown cloud", () => PickManaged(new Need("onprem", false, false, false, false)));
record Need(string Cloud, bool Log, bool OrderedPerKey, bool KafkaApi, bool FanOut);

steps.title: A design-review linter
prompt: The architecture group wants the anti-patterns caught before the review meeting. The tests define
```csharp
record Design(string Broker, int JobSeconds, int Consumers, int Partitions, int RetentionDays, bool AutoAck, bool DbTableQueue, bool SkipLocked);
Write `List<string> Review(Design d)` returning every finding, in this order:
1. `Broker == "kafka"` and `JobSeconds > 300` →
`"kafka: {n}s jobs exceed max.poll.interval.ms (300s) and block their partition; use a queue"`
2. `Broker == "kafka"` and `Consumers > Partitions` →
`"kafka: {Consumers - Partitions} of {Consumers} consumers will sit idle with {Partitions} partitions"`
3. `Broker == "rabbitmq"` and `RetentionDays > 1` →
`"rabbitmq: a queue is not an event store; use a stream or a log for {n}-day retention"`
4. `Broker == "rabbitmq"` and `AutoAck` → `"rabbitmq: autoAck loses in-flight messages on a crash; ack after processing"`
5. `DbTableQueue` and not `SkipLocked` →
`"db queue: claim rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, or workers block each other and take the same row"`
No findings → `["no findings"]`.
solution: findings.Add($"kafka: {d.JobSeconds}s jobs exceed max.poll.interval.ms (300s) and block their partition; use a queue");
findings.Add($"kafka: {d.Consumers - d.Partitions} of {d.Consumers} consumers will sit idle with {d.Partitions} partitions");
findings.Add($"rabbitmq: a queue is not an event store; use a stream or a log for {d.RetentionDays}-day retention");
findings.Add("rabbitmq: autoAck loses in-flight messages on a crash; ack after processing");
findings.Add("db queue: claim rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, or workers block each other and take the same row");
return findings.Count > 0 ? findings : new List<string> { "no findings" };
hints: Five independent `if` statements, each adding one message.
Return `["no findings"]` only when the list is empty.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("the pdf-render design", new List<string>
"kafka: 600s jobs exceed max.poll.interval.ms (300s) and block their partition; use a queue",
"kafka: 4 of 10 consumers will sit idle with 6 partitions",
}, Review(new Design("kafka", JobSeconds: 600, Consumers: 10, Partitions: 6, RetentionDays: 7, AutoAck: false, DbTableQueue: false, SkipLocked: false)));
Dojo.Eq("a healthy Kafka stream", new List<string> { "no findings" }, Review(new Design("kafka", 1, 6, 12, 7, false, false, false)));
Dojo.Eq("RabbitMQ as an archive with autoAck", new List<string>
"rabbitmq: a queue is not an event store; use a stream or a log for 90-day retention",
"rabbitmq: autoAck loses in-flight messages on a crash; ack after processing",
}, Review(new Design("rabbitmq", 2, 20, 0, 90, true, false, false)));
Dojo.Eq("a jobs table without SKIP LOCKED", new List<string> { "db queue: claim rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, or workers block each other and take the same row" },
Review(new Design("postgres", 30, 4, 0, 0, false, true, false)));
Dojo.Eq("a jobs table done right", new List<string> { "no findings" }, Review(new Design("postgres", 30, 4, 0, 0, false, true, true)));
Dojo.Eq("long jobs on RabbitMQ are fine", new List<string> { "no findings" }, Review(new Design("rabbitmq", 1200, 8, 0, 0, false, false, false)));
record Design(string Broker, int JobSeconds, int Consumers, int Partitions, int RetentionDays, bool AutoAck, bool DbTableQueue, bool SkipLocked);
